statement: When an identity key is narrowed so that a measured value no longer changes it, check every place that deduplicates on that key: the old key may have been doing two jobs. 2026-11-09, #700: the GitLab Code Quality fingerprint hashed the raw finding summary, which carries a score, so a score change on an unchanged line read as one fixed plus one new finding. Replacing the summary with a stable identity (fixed for a metric-derived finding, numbers replaced by a placeholder otherwise) fixed that, but the export also skipped any entry whose fingerprint it had already seen. With the narrower key, two different findings at one place that differed only in a number collapsed into one, and the export silently lost a finding. The red guard test written beforehand caught it at the intermediate commit. Fix: deduplicate on the exact summary, and give each distinct summary sharing one identity at one place its ordinal in report order in the hash input, so the export count equals the old one.
